Priya also gave an unusually candid answer about work/life balance, reframing it as 'juggling, not balancing.'

sentences.text: Hey Priya! I know you're slammed this week with the conference coming up, so thank you for making time.
Of course! I've got maybe twenty minutes before I have to go watch my daughter's dance recital rehearsal, but let's go.
Perfect, that's exactly how much time we need. Okay, big picture, anything major happen this month?
Yes, actually, we awarded four new franchise territories last month. That puts us at thirty-five locations total now.
That's huge, where are the new ones?
Boise, two in the Dallas suburbs, and one in Charlotte. The applicant pool for that batch was honestly the strongest we've ever had, like sixty applicants for four spots.
Do you know why the pool's gotten so much stronger?
Honestly? I think it's the LinkedIn stuff we've been doing. We had at least four applicants specifically mention a post about our culture in their application.
That's exactly what we want to hear. Okay, I want to go back to something you mentioned briefly a while ago, your parents' salon. Can you tell me that whole story again, start to finish?
Okay so, my parents came to the US in the early nineties and opened a tiny salon outside Sacramento. Six chairs, one of which was broken half the time.
I basically grew up there. After school I'd do homework in the back room and then sweep hair off the floor for like an hour before we closed.
Did you love it or hate it as a kid?

Both, honestly. I hated the smell of perm solution so much. But I loved watching my mom talk to clients, some of them had been coming for fifteen years, she knew their kids' names, their divorces, everything.
That's such a specific memory. When did the idea of scaling that into something bigger start?
In business school, honestly. I kept thinking, what if that same feeling, the trust, the she knows my name feeling, could exist at scale, not just in one six-chair shop.
And that became Bloom and Bar.
That became Bloom and Bar. My parents actually think it's hilarious that I turned their strip-mall salon into a franchise concept with a business plan and everything.
Okay I love that arc, from sweeping floors to thirty-five locations. That's the post, basically word for word what you just told me.
Please make me sound less rambly than I just was.
I will clean it up, don't worry. Okay, next, I know culture is a huge thing for you. What's something you personally do that most CEOs your size wouldn't bother doing anymore?
I still personally call every single new franchisee on their first day. Not a text, an actual phone call.
Even with thirty-five locations?
Even with thirty-five. It's usually like ten minutes, I just tell them I'm proud of them and remind them why we picked them out of everyone who applied.
Has anyone ever told you that call mattered to them later?
All the time, actually. One franchisee, Renee, in Tulsa, told me a year later that call is the reason she didn't quit during her hardest month.
Okay, hold onto that Renee story, I think there might be a whole separate post in there down the line. For now let's use the day one call habit as its own post.
Good, yes.

Last one, and this is more personal, how are you managing being a mom of two and running a thirty-five location company? I feel like people always ask that in a way that's a little annoying, so tell me your actual honest answer.
My honest answer is I'm not managing it gracefully, I'm managing it messily. Today I answered a franchisee's emergency call while painting my daughter's toenails for the recital.
That's real. That's more real than any polished balance post I've ever seen.
That's the truth of it though. Nobody's balancing anything, we're all just juggling and occasionally dropping something.
Okay, that's a post too, juggling, not balancing. I think that's going to resonate with a lot of the founders in your audience.
I like that a lot more than balance, honestly.

Great, so today I've got four solid ideas, the parents' salon origin story, the day-one welcome call habit, the thirty-five location milestone, and the juggling-not-balancing post. I'll get drafts to you by early next week.
Perfect. Can you grab a couple photos from the conference next week too? I'll have Marcus, our ops guy, snap some.
Yes please, that'll help a lot. Okay, go watch your daughter's rehearsal, thank you Priya!
Thank you, bye!
